Project.name: media-analysis-platform
Project.annotation: GRACE requirements source of truth for the single-user channel-aware target media analysis product model.
Project.keywords: media_asset, stored_object, collection, inbox, selection_snapshot, analysis_run, analysis_run_step, artifact, diagnostic, channel_account, channel_surface, operation_request, telegram, web, mcp, postgres, minio, redis, workers

Purpose.purpose-1: Define the target product architecture for a single human user who can work through Telegram, Web, MCP, and future channels.
Purpose.purpose-2: Keep API-owned product state separate from channel presentation state and worker execution state.
Purpose.purpose-3: Give later Beads a stable requirements target for contracts, storage, orchestration, workers, Web, Telegram, MCP, diagnostics, retention, channel recovery, and evidence gates.

TargetArchitectureReset.bead: Defines the from-scratch target architecture, table set, API operation groups, DTO/type naming, app boundaries, user flows, migration stages, and verification matrix.
TargetArchitectureReset.rule: The product currently has one human user. Do not introduce owners, workspaces, workspace members, or team authorization until a real multi-user requirement exists.
Channel identity is modeled through channel_accounts and channel_surfaces; channels can store presentation and recovery state but cannot own product lifecycle.

The target vocabulary is media_asset, stored_object, collection, inbox, selection_snapshot, analysis_run, analysis_run_step, artifact, diagnostic, channel_account, channel_surface, and operation_request.

The current local database is disposable for the target rebuild. Implementations may delete, recreate, truncate, or rebuild current schema/data and must not spend effort preserving or backfilling existing local rows unless a future production-data requirement is approved.

Existing implementation-era names such as media_item, source, selection, analysis_run_task, owner, and interaction_surface remain migration context only when they appear below. New target work must prefer the target vocabulary unless a compatibility packet explicitly says otherwise.
If any older GRACE section conflicts with the target architecture document, the target architecture document wins until the corresponding migration packet rewrites the older section.

CanonicalVocabulary.term: A durable API-owned record for one user-provided input such as text, URL, file, photo, image, audio, voice, video, or document.
The normalized origin and stored body metadata behind a media_item; source is internal enough to hide adapter transport details from the product surface.
A durable owner-scoped grouping of media_item references used for user organization and later analysis.
The default collection for each owner where new media_item records land unless the caller names another collection.
An immutable ordered snapshot of media_item references, options, and owner scope captured when a user decides what to analyze.
A user-facing run created from one selection; it owns lifecycle, diagnostics, events, and artifact lineage.
A durable result or diagnostic object produced by analysis_run execution and resolved through API-governed access rules.

ModelChain.chain: media_item -> collection/inbox -> immutable selection -> analysis_run -> artifacts
ModelChain.rule: Adapters create and manage media_item and collection state before execution; they do not expose transient submission modes as the product model.
analysis_run creation always references a selection snapshot, never mutable collection contents directly.
Later edits to the inbox or any collection never mutate an existing selection or analysis_run.

OwnerScope.scope: All media_item, collection, selection, analysis_run, artifact, diagnostic, and retention decisions are scoped to an owner identity.
Telegram chat/user, Web account/session, and MCP caller identities are mapped into the same owner model at the API boundary.
OwnerScope.rule: Cross-owner reads, writes, selection reuse, run access, and artifact access are rejected before storage mutation.
Idempotency keys, pagination cursors, optimistic versions, and diagnostic queries are owner-scoped.
Public collection and paginated list envelopes always encode items as an array, including empty collections and empty pages.

Requirement.Action: Create media_item records from Telegram, Web, MCP, and server-side import callers through one API-owned ingestion boundary.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: Supported inputs include text, URL, generic file, photo/image, audio/voice, and video/document; each accepted item records owner, source metadata, content hash when available, size, MIME type, adapter origin, creation time, validation status, retention policy, and diagnostics pointer.

Requirement.Action: Maintain inbox and user collections independently of execution.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: Every owner has a default inbox; callers can list, create, rename, archive, delete, and reorder collection items subject to owner scope and optimistic version checks. Accepted media appends to the next active collection position and must not create duplicate active positions in inbox or user collections.

Requirement.Action: Create immutable selections from explicit ordered media_item references.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: Selection creation validates owner access, media availability, requested analysis options, ordering, duplicate policy, and size limits; the stored snapshot captures item ids, source metadata needed for execution, option values, creator, timestamps, and validation diagnostics.

Requirement.Action: Create analysis_run records only from selections.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: analysis_run creation records selection id, owner, run type, delivery preference, initial queued status, idempotency key, evidence-gate status, and diagnostics channel; execution rows may exist behind the run but must not become the public product surface.

Requirement.Action: Cancel analysis_run records through a cooperative API-owned lifecycle.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: Canceling an unclaimed queued run terminally records canceled and stops queued tasks. Canceling a claimed run records cancel_requested, preserves the claimed task for worker observation, stops unclaimed queued tasks, exposes cancel_requested through worker cancel-check, and forces late worker finalization to resolve as canceled rather than succeeded or failed.

Requirement.Action: Expose artifacts as analysis_run outputs with API-governed preview and download metadata.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: Artifacts include transcript, summary, report, extracted structured data, source manifest, execution log, and diagnostic bundles as applicable; each artifact records owner, run id, kind, content type, size, checksum, storage object key, visibility, retention state, and preview metadata.

Requirement.Action: Preserve rejected or partially processed records as diagnostics instead of silently dropping them.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: Ingestion, selection, run, adapter, worker, artifact, cancellation, retention, and permission failures expose stable diagnostic codes, human-readable messages, provider or adapter context when safe, correlation ids, timestamps, and remediation hints.

Requirement.Action: Apply retention policies consistently across sources, media_item records, selections, runs, artifacts, diagnostics, and deleted collection membership.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: Retention rules define soft delete, hard delete eligibility, artifact expiry, source body expiry, owner export, and audit evidence preservation without orphaning run history.

Requirement.Action: Keep Telegram, Web, and MCP as thin adapters over the same API-owned state.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: Adapters may shape presentation and local transport acknowledgements, but durable inbox, collection, selection, analysis_run, artifact, owner, retention, and diagnostics semantics are owned by the API. Telegram inbox rendering and actions follow collection membership rather than the owner-wide media list. Telegram status copy and action labels are Russian-first and make collection actions plus run-specific result buttons explicit to the user. Web presents simple human wording and must not make internal names such as media_asset, selection_snapshot, analysis_run_step, channel_surface, opaque ids, or diagnostic internals load-bearing UI terms outside explicit admin/debug views.

Requirement.Action: Run report and research analysis from prepared transcript or text-corpus artifacts.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: For audio, video, voice, or other speech media, transcription produces transcript artifacts before report or research execution. Agent-runner consumes ready transcript or text-corpus artifact inputs plus safe metadata, publishes report or research artifacts through analysis_run, and records a prerequisite diagnostic instead of transcribing or processing raw speech media itself when required text input is missing.

Requirement.Action: Persist external interaction surfaces without coupling domain entities to consumer-specific UI.
Requirement.AcceptanceCriteria: Interaction surfaces store owner-scoped channel, surface type, surface key, opaque address, address fingerprint, opaque display state, lifecycle status, version, and timestamps through an internal API. Subject links are stored separately with subject type, subject id, and subject role; event history is append-only. Domain tables must not gain Telegram-specific or consumer-specific message fields, and interaction surface display state must not alter media, collection, selection, analysis_run, artifact, or diagnostic lifecycle.

DeletedArchitecture.rule: Former public routes and schemas centered on immediate transcription execution, grouped pre-run submission state, or public source-set terminology are deleted from the target product architecture.
Former batch toggles and draft semantics are not wrapped, aliased, or preserved as user-facing modes.
Backend execution rows and worker queue messages may remain as implementation details behind analysis_run, but product requirements must name analysis_run as the public run surface.
Historical implementation evidence may be kept only when clearly labeled as deleted architecture or internal execution proof; it must not define target user flows.

Telegram.rule: Telegram accepts messages, files, URLs, media groups, and inline commands as input capture and management gestures over the owner inbox.
Telegram shows the current inbox or collection status after accepted input and offers explicit actions to create a selection and run analysis.
Telegram callback payloads address API-owned media_item, collection, selection, and analysis_run identifiers with versions where mutation is allowed.

Telegram shows background active analysis_run state separately from the current material selection. The current selection can start a new transcription unless the card is focused on an active run. Cancel actions target either the focused active run or, when there is no focus, the latest visible active run by run id plus version.

Telegram main-card result and diagnostics actions are scoped to the analysis_run launched from the current card focus; historical terminal runs do not create generic result actions for a new or unstarted inbox selection.

After a successful Telegram result delivery, the adapter clears only the active inbox or collection membership through the API collection mutation path; immutable selections, analysis_runs, artifacts, and diagnostics remain historical records.
Telegram may persist message mappings through the internal interaction surfaces API, but the API treats those mappings as opaque interaction surfaces rather than Telegram-specific domain fields.

Web.rule: Web is a simple human-facing management surface for browsing materials, creating groups, curating the current selection, launching analysis, and reviewing results, progress, errors, and downloads.

Web calls the public API but normal UI copy must avoid load-bearing internal terms such as media_asset, selection_snapshot, analysis_run_step, channel_surface, raw ids, and diagnostic internals outside explicit admin/debug views.

MCP.rule: MCP exposes tool calls for add_media, list_media, search_media, get_media, remove_media, get_inbox, create_collection, list_collections, get_collection, update_collection, update_collection_items, create_selection, get_selection, run_analysis, list_runs, get_run, cancel_run, retry_run, list_run_events, list_artifacts, get_artifact, get_artifact_preview, refresh_artifact, and get_diagnostics.

EvidenceGates.gate: Planning proof shows the target table set, API operations, DTO/type names, app boundaries, user flows, implementation stages, and test matrix are all covered by docs/architecture/single-user-channel-aware-target-architecture.md.

Contracts prove public vocabulary uses the target names media_asset, stored_object, collection/inbox, selection_snapshot, analysis_run, artifact, diagnostic, channel_account where needed, and channel_surface only for internal channel runtime APIs.

Storage tests prove single-user scope, channel identity boundaries, immutable selection snapshots, lifecycle transitions, idempotency, retention, diagnostics persistence, and channel surface recovery.
API tests prove adapters share the same state and old public product routes are absent from the target contract.

Worker tests prove execution consumes sealed selections, agent-runner consumes ready transcript/text-corpus artifacts for report and research work, and results are reported through analysis_run artifacts and diagnostics.

Telegram, Web, and MCP tests prove management-first flows without user-facing batch toggles or immediate execution-only assumptions; Web tests also prove normal UI copy stays human and avoids internal technical vocabulary.
Compose or equivalent runtime proof verifies end-to-end ingestion, selection, run, artifact, diagnostics, and retention behavior.

BeadsTrace.bead: Public contracts and schemas now expose the canonical inbox-first vocabulary.
Server storage/API orchestration is implemented for the canonical media_item to artifact chain.
Worker execution now runs behind analysis_run with sealed selection consumption.
Telegram now operates over explicit selection/run semantics on the API-owned inbox.
Web management UI now covers inbox, collections, run detail, artifact use, and sealed-selection regressions.
MCP tools now match the owner-scoped canonical API surface.
Runtime-final compose proof exists for end-to-end inbox, selection, run, artifact, diagnostics, owner denial, and retention behavior.
Executable coverage inventory is documented and runnable, with remaining measurement gaps explicit.
GRACE packet truth now matches the actual closed state of the repo.
The final ordered closure matrix is published and synchronized with the current verification truth.
analysis_run cancellation now uses cooperative cancel_requested semantics before terminal worker finalization.
Telegram active-run cards no longer dead-end new selections or background cancellation.
Telegram selection and transcription card UX contracts are documented as a durable architecture plan.
Generic external surface API contracts are documented without coupling domain state to Telegram-specific UI needs.
Interaction Surfaces terminology refines the external surface contract around channel, surface type, address, display state, and lifecycle status.
Interaction Surfaces table design is finalized as surfaces, subject links, and append-only events.
Single-user channel-aware target architecture is fixed as the new from-scratch product plan, with child Beads for implementation execution.

NonGoals.item: Reintroducing old public product route vocabulary as an alias layer.
Preserving grouped pre-run submission state as the user-facing collection model.
Letting Telegram, Web, or MCP own durable product state independently of the API.
Changing application code in this Bead.
